title: Virginia's 6th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: Virginia's 6th Congressional District covers the Shenandoah Valley, Roanoke Valley, and parts of central Virginia including Charlottesville, Lynchburg, and Harrisonburg. The race pits incumbent Republican Rep. Ben Cline, first elected in 2018 and a staunch conservative, against Democratic nominee Beth Macy, a best-selling author and former journalist making her first run for political office. The race gained additional significance after the Virginia Supreme Court struck down a 2026 ballot referendum that would have redrawn congressional maps to favor Democrats, leaving the current Republican-leaning district boundaries intact. Cline is favored in the district, which voted for Donald Trump by 24 points in 2024 and re-elected Cline by 28 points, but Macy has mounted a well-funded campaign emphasizing economic populism and rural community concerns.
polling_note: No direct head-to-head general election polling for Cline vs. Macy was publicly available as of mid-2026. A G. Elliot Morris MRP analysis published April 14, 2026 by Cardinal News estimated Trump's approval in the 6th District at 48.3% approve / 51.7% disapprove, suggesting a potentially competitive environment but did not test the specific matchup.

candidates.name: Ben Cline
candidates.summary: Ben Cline is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Virginia's 6th District, first elected in 2018. He previously served in the Virginia House of Delegates from 2002 to 2018 and worked as an assistant commonwealth's attorney. Cline is a conservative Republican who serves on the House Judiciary and Budget committees and has focused on reducing government regulation, protecting Second Amendment rights, and supporting border security.

forecast.rationale: No head-to-head general election polling is available, so confidence is necessarily medium. The district fundamentals still strongly favor the incumbent Republican: the Virginia Supreme Court struck down a 2026 referendum that would have redrawn lines to favor Democrats, leaving the current Republican-leaning boundaries intact; Donald Trump won the district by 24 points in 2024; and Ben Cline was re-elected by 28 points. Cline is a four-term incumbent with a long pre-Congress career in the district (Virginia House of Delegates 2002–2018). The Democratic challenger, Beth Macy, is a best-selling author and first-time candidate described as well-funded with a message of economic populism, but there is no polling to test whether that message is moving voters. A G. Elliot Morris MRP analysis (Cardinal News, April 2026) estimated Trump's district-level approval at 48.3% approve vs. 51.7% disapprove — a modestly negative net approval despite the +24 vote margin, which hints at possible softness but is not a direct vote-choice signal. Without head-to-head polling, the strong recent Republican voting record anchors the forecast in likely Republican territory rather than safe, as a well-funded challenger in a shifting environment could narrow the margin.
